\section*{Question 3}

The graph of the function \(f\) shown above consists of six line segments. Let \(g\) be the function given by \(g(x)=\int_{0}^{x} f(t) d t\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find \(g(4), g^{\prime}(4)\), and \(g^{\prime \prime}(4)\).
\item[(b)] Does \(g\) have a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither at \(x=1\) ? Justify your answer.
\end{itemize}
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/88ffb53c-ea89-4b42-b8f4-206fdbb7639e-1.jpg?height=529&width=924&top_left_y=367&top_left_x=1038)
\begin{itemize}
\item[(c)] Suppose that \(f\) is defined for all real numbers \(x\) and is periodic with a period of length 5. The graph above shows two periods of \(f\). Given that \(g(5)=2\), find \(g(10)\) and write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of \(g\) at \(x=108\).
\item[(a)] \(g(4)=\int_{0}^{4} f(t) d t=3\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& g^{\prime}(4)=f(4)=0 \\
& g^{\prime \prime}(4)=f^{\prime}(4)=-2
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)] \(g\) has a relative minimum at \(x=1\) because \(g^{\prime}=f\) changes from negative to positive at \(x=1\).
\item[(c)] \(g(0)=0\) and the function values of \(g\) increase by 2 for every increase of 5 in \(x\).
\[
g(10)=2 g(5)=4
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
g(108) & =\int_{0}^{105} f(t) d t+\int_{105}^{108} f(t) d t \\
& =2 \lg (5)+g(3)=44
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
g^{\prime}(108)=f(108)=f(3)=2
\]
An equation for the line tangent to the graph of \(g\) at \(x=108\) is \(y-44=2(x-108)\).
\end{itemize}
